notes.1.9.6.1: converterit (“if we agree”) makes no sense as it stands and is read as convenerit; medicamenta is read as medicamento.

nodes.text: You ask how he will make a friend quickly. I will tell you, if we agree that I pay you at once what I owe and that, as far as this letter is concerned, we are quits. Hecaton says: “I will show you a love-potion without drugs, without herbs, without any witch’s spell: if you want to be loved, love.” And not only the practice of an old and settled friendship holds great pleasure, but also the beginning and acquiring of a new one.

From my place at Nomentum I greet you and bid you have a sound mind, that is, have all the gods propitious; and whoever has made himself propitious to himself has them appeased and favourable. Set aside for the present the view some hold, that a god is assigned to each one of us as a tutor, not indeed one of the regular rank, but one of this lower grade, from the number of those whom Ovid calls “gods of the common people”. Yet I want you to set this aside in such a way as to remember that our ancestors, who believed it, were Stoics; for they gave each person both a Genius and a Juno.
